channel.title: Lumeshot
channel.description: Updates for Lumeshot, a screenshot and screen-recording tool for macOS.

item.description:
Two fixes: one to the annotation editor's finish buttons, one to the error an SFTP destination shows when it is given the wrong kind of key.
## The editor's finish buttons are readable again
After a capture, the editor's toolbar ends in four buttons — **Cancel**, **Copy**, **Save**, and **Upload** — that decide what happens to the annotated image. They had no icons and were packed into the same row as every drawing tool, so at the editor's window size their labels were squeezed down to about one letter each and read as a meaningless "C C … U". There was no obvious way to say you were done.
The four buttons now carry icons alongside full labels, **Save** and **Upload** are shown as prominent (blue) buttons, and the editor opens wide enough — and no longer shrinks below the width the toolbar needs — that the labels can never be truncated again. What each does is unchanged: **Save** writes to disk (and history), **Upload** saves and uploads, **Copy** puts the image on the clipboard, and **Cancel** discards the capture.
## A clearer error for an RSA SFTP key
An SFTP destination configured with an **RSA** private key used to fail with an opaque authentication error. It now names the cause — the SSH library can only sign with the legacy `ssh-rsa` (SHA-1) algorithm that OpenSSH 8.8 and newer reject by default — and points you at using an Ed25519 key instead.

One fix, to something you would have seen every time you clicked a notification.
## Clicking a notification no longer opens Settings
Clicking **Capture complete** revealed the screenshot in Finder and then put the Settings window in front of it. Clicking **Uploaded** opened the link and did the same. Both notifications were doing the right thing — the Settings window was uninvited, and it covered the thing you had just asked for.
macOS reports the app being activated by a notification click the same way it reports a click on the Dock icon, and Lumeshot opens Settings for the latter because a menu-bar app has no other window to show. It now tells the two apart.
Clicking the Dock icon still opens Settings, including straight after dismissing a notification.

No changes to the app. This release is identical to v0.1.15 and exists so the automatic updater has something to update *to*.
v0.1.15 introduced Sparkle, but a copy of it finds only its own entry in the feed, so nothing about the download-and-install path could be exercised until a newer release existed. This is that release.
If you are reading this inside Lumeshot's update window, the part that needed testing has already worked: the app checked the feed, found this version, and fetched these notes. Installing it exercises the rest — verifying the signature, replacing the app in place, and relaunching.
If you are on v0.1.15 there is nothing to gain by updating, beyond confirming that updating works.
